figure.name: Eugene V. Debs
figure.role: American labor leader, socialist candidate, organizer, speaker, and prisoner for anti-war speech.
figure.hook: Debs = U.S. labor politics and American socialism.
whyHere: Debs belongs here because he brings the road into American democratic life: railroads, unions, strikes, elections, courts, prisons, and public speech.
He matters because socialism in the United States is not only a foreign scare-word. It also has a labor, free-speech, voting, and class-solidarity history.
figure.cleanIdea: Debs asks whether democracy can hear working people when wealth, courts, employers, and war pressure push the other way. He is the American labor doorway because he connects railroad work, union defeat, Socialist Party campaigns, public speech, anti-war prosecution, and class solidarity in one life.

ideas.title: Unionism
ideas.plainDefinition: Unionism means workers organizing together to bargain, strike, vote, and force employers and government to hear them.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, unionism is the practical doorway from individual frustration to organized labor power.
ideas.whyMatters: Unionism matters because socialism in the United States often enters politics through labor organization, not abstract theory first. The worker does not face the employer as an equal isolated individual; the union is one way workers create bargaining power together.
ideas.carefulVersion: A union is not automatically socialist, and every union is not automatically just. Some unions have been democratic and solidaristic; some have been exclusionary, conservative, corrupt, or narrow. The important lesson is that unionism turns labor from private complaint into organized power.

ideas.title: American Socialism
ideas.plainDefinition: American socialism is the U.S. labor and electoral tradition that used socialist language for unions, democracy, public ownership debates, anti-war speech, and class politics.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, American socialism is not imported as a cartoon. It is part of U.S. labor and democratic history.
ideas.whyMatters: American socialism matters because it keeps the project from letting anti-communist shorthand erase U.S. labor history. Debs shows that socialism in America included elections, courts, unions, prisons, anti-war speech, and constitutional public argument.
ideas.carefulVersion: American socialism is not one thing. It includes labor parties, electoral campaigns, public ownership debates, democratic-socialist language, union organizing, and anti-capitalist critique. Do not collapse it into Soviet communism, and do not pretend it has no history here.

ideas.title: Labor Politics
ideas.plainDefinition: Labor politics means workers using unions, parties, strikes, campaigns, and public speech to change economic and political power.
ideas.context: In the Debs path, labor politics connects shop-floor conflict to elections and public argument.
ideas.whyMatters: Labor politics matters because it shows democracy is not only voting. It is also the struggle over whether ordinary workers can organize power at work, in courts, in parties, in public speech, and in the street.
ideas.carefulVersion: Labor politics can be reformist or radical, narrow or broad, democratic or machine-like. The point is not to romanticize labor automatically. The point is to study how people without large property try to build leverage against people and institutions that do have it.
